fresh_run_confirmation.note_on_first_attempt: A first full run attempt (same executable boundary, same fresh venv) was manually interrupted after ~350/2629 mutants processed, upon observing repeated `BadTestExecutionCommandsException` tracebacks in the console output for scattered individual mutants. Root-cause investigation (direct reproduction with MUTANT_UNDER_TEST set) confirmed this is a GENUINE, mutation-induced conftest.py import-time collection failure (e.g., a `/` -> `*` operator mutation in `_find_repo_root`, called at module level by conftest.py's own authority-resolution fixtures via tooling/ride_mutmut_shim.py's own documented, approved compatibility design for P3-PY-MUT-BASELINE-B-MAJ-01) -- NOT an infrastructure defect, stale test-selection artifact, or environment problem. Per the shim's own docstring, this specific case (pytest exit code 4 outside the one-time forced-fail sanity check) is intentionally left fatal to the mutant's own forked child process, byte-for-byte identical to unmodified mutmut 3.7.0; the parent process's own fork/exit-code monitoring then correctly records the mutant as killed (the mutation demonstrably broke test collection, an unambiguous kill signal), which is the semantically correct mutation-testing outcome, not a data-integrity defect. The workspace was fully cleaned and the run was restarted from a clean state; this note is preserved for auditability.
fresh_run_confirmation.single_worker_rationale: Evidence-005 diagnosed substantial false-positive timeout inflation from parallel-worker resource contention (88 raw timeouts, only 5 confirmed genuine). --max-children 1 was used for this measurement to obtain a deterministic, single-worker formal run, per instruction -- not for throughput.
fresh_run_confirmation.methodology_note_display_step_crash: The `run` CLI process reached 2629/2629 processed mutants and printed its final rate line ("2.90 mutations/second"), then exited silently WITHOUT printing its own post-processing 'Mutant results' summary listing (no traceback, no error at the top level). This is the SAME cosmetic display-step behavior documented in evidence-005.json's own fresh_run_confirmation -- confirmed here identically: `python -m tooling export-cicd-stats` and `python -m tooling results --all true` both successfully read the SAME underlying persisted per-mutant result store and returned complete, internally consistent data (killed=2243, survived=384, timeout=2, total=2629, all other statuses=0, sum exactly equal to total). This does not constitute a failure to reach natural completion.

timeout_triage.protocol: For each raw timeout candidate: (1) delete mutants/ workspace and .mutmut-cache; (2) regenerate a fully fresh workspace; (3) run the mutant in isolated `python -m tooling run --max-children 1 <id>` mode, record result #1; (4) delete mutants/ again; (5) independently regenerate another fully fresh workspace; (6) rerun the same mutant, record result #2. Classification: timeout+timeout -> CONFIRMED_TIMEOUT; killed+killed -> resolved KILLED; survived+survived -> resolved SURVIVED; any disagreement -> UNSTABLE_TIMEOUT_TRIAGE (no majority vote, no third tie-break run, no guess).

per_mutant_triage_results.note: Same mutant identity Evidence-005's own correction (P3-PY-MUT-STEP9-003-A-MAJ-01) confirmed as a genuine deterministic timeout at that boundary -- consistent finding, independently re-confirmed at this boundary.

This mutant is called at conftest.py module-import time (SWING_DISTANCE_INPUT_CONTRACT / REGIME_INPUT_CONTRACT); it raised the same genuine, mutation-induced conftest.py collection failure diagnosed above, which fatally crashes the forked child process and is correctly recorded as killed by mutmut's own fork/exit-code monitoring. In the full-run's shared-resource context it apparently manifested as a raw 'timeout' (plausibly the exception surfaced slowly enough to cross the computed wall-time limit under full-run conditions); in BOTH independent single-mutant isolated reproductions it consistently manifested as an immediate crash/kill, not a timeout. Per the strict protocol, this resolves to KILLED and folds into the final killed count -- it is NOT counted as confirmed_timeout and NOT counted as unstable_timeout_triage, since both isolated reproductions agreed with each other (killed + killed).
